claim: The official tourist office route through Menton old town links Saint-Michel Archangel Basilica (1639), the Pénitents Blancs Chapel (1680-1687) and the Vieux Château cemetery, with notable burials of architect Hans-Georg Tersling and rugby inventor William Webb Ellis.
quote: Saint-Michel Archangel Basilica (built 1639): A Baroque masterpiece with a 53m bell tower... Vieux Château Cemetery: Overlooks the bay with notable burials including architect Hans-Georg Tersling and rugby inventor William Webb Ellis

claim: The Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange was built between 1640 and 1653 on the foundations of two earlier 14th-15th century churches dedicated to Saint Michel, and is a minor basilica still serving as the Catholic parish church of Menton's historic core.
quote: The Basilica of Saint-Michel-Archange of Menton is a minor basilica and a Catholic parish church located in the heart of the historic center of Menton. It was erected between 1640 and 1653 on the vestiges of two churches from the 14th and 15th centuries

claim: The Parvis Saint-Michel's calade was rebuilt in 2006 with 250,000 pebbles selected one by one from the Careï and Borrigo beaches, laid across 170 m² to form the Grimaldi arms and an H for Prince Honoré of Monaco.
quote: The Parvis was completely renovated in 2006, requiring 250,000 pebbles to reconstitute the 170 m². These small stones were selected one by one for their color and shape from the beaches of Careï and Borrigo... arms of the Grimaldi family as well as a letter H for 'Prince Honoré'

claim: The Rampes Saint-Michel were commissioned by Prince Honoré III in 1753 to link the seafront to the Basilique Saint-Michel; the upper section is a listed historical monument and the lower stretch dates from a Second World War restoration.
quote: The Escaliers, also known as Les Rampes Saint-Michel, were built on the orders of Prince Honoré III, who ordered them built in 1753. The upper part of the ramps is listed as a historical monument and dates from the middle of the 18th century, while the lower part dates from the Second World War

claim: The Basilique Saint-Michel is open Monday-Friday 15:00-17:00 and Saturday 10:00-12:00 and 15:00-17:00, closed Sunday except for the 11:00 Sunday mass, with free entry.
quote: The basilica is open Monday through Friday between 3 pm and 5 pm, on Saturday between 10 am and 12 pm and between 3 pm and 5 pm, and is closed on Sunday. However, it is accessible on Sundays at 11:00 am for mass

claim: The Chapelle des Pénitents Blancs (also called Chapelle de l'Immaculée Conception), built from 1680 and consecrated in 1687 on land donated by Prince Louis I Grimaldi, is a Baroque Catholic Reformation chapel listed as a Monument Historique in 1947 and sits adjacent to the Basilique.
quote: The chapel of the Immaculate Conception, or White Penitents, was built from 1680, in the Capitol district, on land outside the walls of the medieval city, donated by Prince Louis I Grimaldi... It was declared a Historical Monument in 1947

claim: The Cimetière du Vieux-Château is open 07:00-19:00 from April to October (08:00-17:00 in winter), free, sits 5 minutes from the Basilique at the start of Boulevard du Garavan, and contains a golden-domed Russian Orthodox chapel reflecting Menton's 19th-century convalescent community.
quote: Hours: 7 a.m.–7 p.m. (April–October); 8 a.m.–5 p.m. (November–March)... approximately a 5-minute walk from the Basilique Saint-Michel... A Russian Orthodox chapel with a golden dome reflects the 19th-century Russian community

claim: Lonely Planet recommends meandering up through the old town to the hilltop Cimetière du Vieux-Château for sweeping views over the old town and port — built on the site of Menton's demolished medieval château.
quote: For great views of the old town and the port, meander all the way up through the historic quarter to this hilltop cemetery

claim: Quai Bonaparte was inaugurated on 14 August after a €4.5 million refit between the Bastion and Victoria roundabouts, adding tiled paving, a sea-side cycle path, LED lighting and plantings of centenarian olive trees, palms and citrus along the old-town waterfront.
quote: the requalification of Quai Bonaparte on August 14th, situated between the Bastion roundabout and the Victoria traffic circle. The €4.5 million project featured quality finishes including tiled paving on the built-up side... centennial olive trees, palms, citrus

claim: Rue Longue is the main artery of Menton's old town, running parallel to Quai Bonaparte between the Saint-Julien gate (east) and Saint-Antoine gate (southwest) on the line of the ancient Roman Via Julia Augusta.
quote: Rue Longue, parallel to the Quai Bonaparte, is the main artery of the old town, running between the Saint-Julien gate in the East and the Saint-Antoine gate in the Southwest, following the route of the ancient Roman road Julia Augusta

claim: The signature postcard view of Menton — pastel houses stacked beneath the Basilique with the Rampes Saint-Michel as focal point — is captured from the jetty at the end of Quai Napoléon III / Quai Impératrice Eugénie, best in morning light.
quote: The most famous view in Menton is found at the end of Quai Impératrice Eugénie, where Menton's colorful houses rise against the hillside, with the Basilique Saint-Michel Archange and the Rampe Saint-Michel creating the perfect focal points

claim: Serre de la Madone is open April 1 to October 31 daily 10am-6pm except Mondays, with adult self-guided admission at €10 and €7 for ages 6-18, while guided tours cost €15 / €11 and require advance booking.
quote: 10€ Adults over 18 years of age... Self-guided tour... Guided tour... Adults €15 / Children (6-18) €11

claim: Serre de la Madone sits at 74 route du Val de Gorbio, a few kilometres inland from the coast with a bus stop within 500m, making it reachable but not walkable from Menton centre.
quote: 74 route du Val de Gorbio, 06500 Menton... a few kilometres from the coast... Near public transportation with bus stop within 500 meters

claim: Val Rahmeh-Menton botanical garden is run by the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle (MNHN), open April-October 10am-6pm closed Tuesdays plus closed May 1, on roughly 1.5 hectares with about 1,800 subtropical and Mediterranean species.
quote: From April 1 to October 31: 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open every day except Tuesdays, May 1, and December 25... 1,800 subtropical, tropical and Mediterranean species

claim: Val Rahmeh was entrusted to the MNHN in 1967 and operates as a public botanical garden at Avenue Saint-Jacques on the Garavan side of Menton.
quote: entrusted to the MNHN (Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle) since 1967

claim: Jardin Maria Serena is accessible only by guided tour booked via Menton's Office de Tourisme, with mandatory reservation, adult ticket €10, reduced €7, children under 6 free, meeting in front of the main gate.
quote: Full price: €10.00... Children 6+ and students: €7.00... Under 6: Free... Devant le grand portail du jardin

claim: Maria Serena's guided tours typically run Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays 10:00-11:30 from a villa designed by Charles Garnier, reputed to be the most temperate garden in France with palms, cycads and tropical species.
quote: Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays from 10:00 to 11:30... reputed to be the most temperate in France... villa Maria Serena was built in 1886 on the plans of Charles Garnier

claim: Fontana Rosa requires a booked guided tour through the Office de Tourisme at €6 per person, meeting at 6 Avenue Blasco-Ibañez; bookings handled by phone +33 4 92 41 76 76.
quote: The guided tour costs €6.00 for all audiences... Reservations are mandatory... Entrée du jardin... 6 Avenue Blasco-Ibañez, 06500 Menton

claim: Fontana Rosa, created by Spanish novelist Vicente Blasco-Ibañez in 1921 and classified Monument Historique in 1990, is a Valencian-style ceramic 'jardin des Romanciers' under ongoing restoration by the city.
quote: créé en 1921 par Vicente Blasco-Ibañez... classé Monument Historique depuis 1990... jardin des Romanciers

claim: Jardin des Colombières, the private Ferdinand Bac villa-garden at 312 Route de Super Garavan, opens to guided visits each Wednesday at 2pm (9am in July-August) from April to October, €20 per person, capped at 15 visitors, online booking only.
quote: Wednesdays at 2:00 PM (9:00 AM in July-August), April through October... €20 per person... 15 people per visit... 312 Route de Super Garavan

claim: Les Colombières paths are steep, uneven and unsuitable for young children or visitors with mobility issues, with the upper entrance the only meeting point and pets not allowed.
quote: garden paths are often steep and uneven... not recommended for young children and anyone with mobility problems... Upper entrance only

claim: Clos du Peyronnet (Waterfield Garden) only opens for public guided tours on Fridays of September and October at 3pm, at €20 per adult and €14 reduced, capped at 20 guests — meaning it is NOT visitable in May 2026.
quote: each Friday of September and October at 3pm with a certified guide in English and French... 20€ per adult, or 14€ per student or child... maximum of 20 guests

claim: Clos du Peyronnet has been owned by the Waterfield family for more than a century and is regarded as the best surviving English-style Arts and Crafts garden on the French Riviera.
quote: the property has been owned and developed by super-plantsman William Waterfield and his family for more than a century

claim: Menton's six historic gardens — Maria Serena, Serre de la Madone, Fontana Rosa, Clos du Peyronnet, Val Rahmeh and Les Colombières — are collectively promoted by the Office de Tourisme as the city's 'Jardins Remarquables' circuit.
quote: Maria Serena, Serre de la Madone, Fontana Rosa, Clos du Peyronet, Val Rahmeh-Menton Botanical Garden and Les Colombières Garden are almost all open to the general public

claim: The Ricciotti Wunderman building has been closed since Storm Adrian (October 2018) flooded the reserves to 1.5m, damaging ~70% of ~2,000 stored works; reopening is not expected before the end of the decade (2030+), with two years of preservation-plan modifications plus three years of construction still required.
quote: La tempête Adrian, en 2018, a fait pénétrer l'eau de mer dans les réserves du musée jusqu'à une hauteur de 1,50 mètre, endommageant environ 70 % des quelque 2 000 œuvres qui y étaient stockées.

claim: As of 2026 the Ricciotti building remains shuttered seven years on; the Severin Wunderman Foundation is threatening restitution of the 1,800-piece donation on grounds that the permanent-exhibition condition is breached, while a dispute with insurer SMACL is before the Nice administrative tribunal.
quote: Sept ans après la tempête Adrian d'octobre 2018, les façades du musée Jean-Cocteau font toujours face à la mer sans accueillir de visiteurs.

claim: Roughly 100 masterworks from the Wunderman donation are on view as 'Les chefs-d'œuvre du musée Jean Cocteau Collection Séverin Wunderman' at the Galerie des musées, Palais de l'Europe (8 avenue Boyer), Tuesday–Saturday 10–12 and 14–18, from 12 April 2025 through 27 August 2026.
quote: Galerie des musées – Collection Jean Cocteau Séverin Wunderman, Palais de l'Europe, 8 avenue Boyer 06500 Menton. Mardi à samedi 10h–12h et 14h–18h.

claim: Le Bastion (Musée Jean Cocteau, Quai Napoléon III) is open daily 10:00–12:30 and 14:00–18:00, closed Tuesdays and on 1 Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov and 25 Dec; the current temporary show 'Portraits autoportraits — Jean Cocteau et ses amis' runs 13 December 2025 to 8 June 2026.
quote: Le Bastion est ouvert tous les jours de 10h à 12h30 et de 14h à 18h, fermé le mardi et les 1er janvier, 1er mai, 1er novembre et 25 décembre.

claim: Le Bastion charges €5 full / €3.75 reduced, with free admission every first Sunday of the month; the museum occupies a 17th-century fortin at the end of the jetty between the port and the Promenade du Soleil.
quote: Plein tarif : 5 €, tarif réduit : 3,75 €. Entrée gratuite le premier dimanche de chaque mois.

claim: The Salle des Mariages at the Hôtel de Ville (17 rue de la République), decorated by Cocteau 1956–1958 with Orpheus/Eurydice and a Menton wedding procession, is open weekdays 8:30–12:00 and 14:00–16:30, closed weekends and holidays; admission €2 full / €1 reduced / free under-18.
quote: Plein tarif : 2 €; Demi-tarif : 1 € (étudiants, enseignants, seniors de plus de 65 ans, familles nombreuses); Gratuit pour les enfants de moins de 18 ans.

claim: Guided tours of the Salle des Mariages depart every Thursday from Place de la Mairie for €4 per person.
quote: Des visites guidées sont proposées tous les jeudis, Place de la Mairie, au tarif de 4 euros.

claim: The Musée des Beaux-Arts in the Palais de Carnolès (3 avenue de la Madone), former summer residence of the Princes of Monaco set in a citrus orchard, holds paintings from the 13th century to the present and is open daily except Tuesdays and public holidays, 10–12 and 14–18.
quote: Ouvert tous les jours sauf le mardi et les jours fériés, de 10h à 12h et de 14h à 18h.

claim: The Musée de Préhistoire Régionale (9 rue Lorédan-Larchey) is free and open daily 10–12 and 14–18 except Tuesdays and holidays; expert-led tours run the first Wednesday of the month at 14:30 for €4.
quote: Entrée gratuite. Ouvert tous les jours de 10h à 12h et de 14h à 18h, fermé le mardi et les jours fériés.

claim: Plage des Sablettes is composed of very fine gravel (gravillons très fins), spans ~350 m at Quai Bonaparte between Vieux Port and Garavan, and is supervised in summer with a rescue post.
quote: gravillons très fins ... spanning approximately 350 meters ... surveillée pendant la saison estivale ... rescue post located near the private beach sections

claim: Plage du Fossan is a public non-smoking beach of pebbles with sandy patches, lifeguarded in summer, with wooden boardwalk, lockers and family rentals.
quote: Plage du Fossan ... Pebbles with sandy patches ... Public (non-smoking area) ... Yes (summer) ... Wooden boardwalk, lockers, sports facilities, pirate ships and pedal horse rentals

claim: Plage Hawaï sits 1 km from the Italian border, allows dogs and fishing, and is marketed as 'the last beach in France' with limited dining (bring a picnic).
quote: Located just 1km from Italy, this quiet, narrow pebble beach allows dogs and fishing. It's 'the last beach in France' ... Limited dining options suggest bringing a picnic.

claim: Menton sea temperature averages 17.9°C across May, with late-May (May 22–27) averaging ~19.8°C, ranging from 16.3°C to 22.5°C.
quote: Overall May Average: 17.9°C ... Late May Specifics (May 22-27): Average: Approximately 19.8°C ... Minimum: 16.3°C (May 22) ... Maximum: 22.5°C (May 27)

claim: Phase 1 of a €4.1M wave-attenuator coastal-protection project on Plage des Sablettes finished before summer 2026 (inaugurated 13 April 2026); Phase 2 (pontoon + Plage Hawaï renaturalization) runs Oct 2026–Apr 2027.
quote: Phase 1 (Completed): January 2026 to June 2026 - Creation of a wave attenuator ... inaugurated on Monday, April 13, 2026. Phase 2: October 2026 to April 2027 - Work on the pontoon and Plage Hawai

claim: Menton's private beach clubs include Les Sablettes Beach Club (with online booking), CalaBro Beach Club, La Cabane Plage, La Dolce Vita and La Pergola, typically open May–September 9am–7pm at €20–80/day.
quote: CalaBro Beach Club ... La Cabane Plage ... La Dolce Vita ... La Pergola ... Les Sablettes Beach Club ... operate seasonally from May through September, generally welcoming visitors between 9 AM and 7 PM, with daily rates ranging from approximately €20-€80

claim: Menton Nautique Club at the Vieux Port rents single kayaks (€15–20/h), double kayaks (€25–35/h) and paddleboards (€15–18/h), though promenade construction has suspended rentals as of mid-2025.
quote: Menton Nautique Club is located on the Vieux Port and offers rentals of single kayaks (15-20€/h), double kayaks (25-35€/h), and paddleboards (15-18€/h) ... due to construction work on the promenade de la mer, the nautical center is no longer able to offer rentals

claim: Public beaches along the Promenade du Soleil (including Plage du Marché between Fossan and Casino Barrière) are lifeguarded only 1 July–31 August.
quote: All the beaches are monitored by lifeguards in summer, from July 1st to August 31st ... Plage du Marché stretches between Plage du Fossan and the Casino Barrière, right along the Promenade du Soleil

claim: Citron de Menton has held IGP (Indication Géographique Protégée) status since 21 September 2015 — not AOP — across Menton, Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, Gorbio, Castellar and Sainte-Agnès, within 7 km of the coast and below 390 m altitude.
quote: Citron de Menton IGP — aire géographique: Menton, Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, Gorbio, Castellar, Sainte-Agnès; vergers à 7 km maximum du littoral et en dessous de 390 m d'altitude.

claim: The IGP cahier des charges requires hand-picking ripe on the tree, bans post-harvest waxing and chemical treatments, and demands a sugar/citric-acid ratio between 1.2 and 2.2 — giving the sweet-tart, non-bitter profile prized by starred chefs.
quote: Cueilli à la main à maturité sur l'arbre, sans cire ni traitement post-récolte; rapport sucre/acide compris entre 1,2 et 2,2 — sucré et acidulé sans amertume, le caviar de la Riviera.

claim: Fruit must measure 53–90 mm diameter, contain at least 25% juice by weight, and carry a finely-granulated zest exceptionally rich in essential oils — the trait pastry chefs and distillers chase.
quote: Calibre entre 53 et 90 mm; jus représentant au minimum 25 % du poids total; zeste finement granuleux libérant un parfum puissant aux essences aromatiques très prononcées.

claim: Maison Herbin's artisan jam fabrique at 2 Rue du Vieux Collège runs free guided tours Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 with complimentary tasting; self-guided visits Mon–Fri 9:30–12:00 and 14:00–17:30.
quote: 2 Rue du Vieux Collège, 06500 Menton. Visite libre du lundi au vendredi de 9h30 à 12h et de 14h à 17h30. Visite guidée lundi, mercredi et vendredi à 10h30. Dégustation offerte.

claim: Maison Herbin, founded 1974, holds the Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant label and produces 180–200 jam varieties in front of visitors, having won gold medals at the Salon de l'Agriculture for citrus jams.
quote: Maison Herbin, confiturier artisanal depuis 1974, labellisée Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant; entre 180 et 200 variétés de confitures fabriquées sous les yeux des visiteurs; médailles d'or au Concours Général Agricole.

claim: Maison Gannac (branded as 'La Maison du Citron') operates a year-round boutique at 10 rue Saint-Michel, Menton, open daily 10:00–19:00, selling IGP lemons, jams, olive oils, limoncello and other lemon spirits from their own orchards.
quote: Boutique Maison Gannac — 10 rue Saint-Michel, 06500 Menton, ouverte tous les jours de 10h à 19h; citrons IGP, confitures, huiles d'olive, limoncello, liqueurs issus de nos vergers.

claim: Maison Gannac's guided orchard tour and tasting (40 min tour + 20 min tasting of marmalades, lemonade, limoncello, olive oil) runs with a free shuttle from the 10 rue Saint-Michel boutique — primarily during the Fête du Citron window but bookable off-season by request.
quote: Guided tour of the orchard (40 min) and tasting session (20 min) of jams, lemonade, limoncello, olive oil; free shuttle from the boutique at 10 rue Saint-Michel.

claim: La Citronneraie / Jardin du Mas Flofaro on the Annonciade hill — a 16th-century property holding the Jardin Remarquable label since 2008 — contains 800+ plant species alongside its lemon and olive trees; visits are by appointment year-round via the Menton heritage office.
quote: Citronneraie du Mas Flofaro, colline de l'Annonciade; label Jardin Remarquable depuis 2008; plus de 800 espèces végétales; visites toute l'année sur rendez-vous via le service Patrimoine de la Ville de Menton (04 92 10 33 66).

claim: La Citronneraie Mas Flofaro is family-run and cultivates the IGP Menton lemon using traditional ancestral methods with century-old trees in a microclimate between sea and mountains; reservation required, walking shoes recommended.
quote: Family-run lemon grove perpetuating ancestral know-how; century-old trees in a unique microclimate between sea and mountains; reservation required, walking shoes recommended.

claim: Au Pays du Citron, founded 2008 by Fabrice and Sonia Puech, operates its flagship boutique in Menton old town stocking ~200 Menton-IGP-lemon references; its Limoncello de Menton accounts for 40% of sales at ~50,000 bottles/year.
quote: Au Pays du Citron, boutique pionnière fondée en 2008 par Fabrice et Sonia Puech à Menton; environ 200 références à base de Citron de Menton IGP; Limoncello de Menton, 50 000 bouteilles par an, 40 % du chiffre d'affaires.

claim: 'L'Arche des Confitures' is Maison Herbin's tasting-and-shop concept in the pedestrian heart of Menton, where visitors discover hundreds of regional jam varieties from the artisan jam-maker.
quote: L'Arche des Confitures de la Maison Herbin — confiturerie artisanale mentonnaise au cœur de la zone piétonne; des milliers de pots et des centaines de variétés de confitures régionales.

claim: TER trains run Menton–Monaco–Monte-Carlo direct with 17 daily services, ~10 minutes for the 9 km hop.
quote: There are 17 trains per day between Menton and Monaco. The fastest train covers the 9 km distance in 10 minutes.

claim: Menton–Ventimiglia by TER is about 9 minutes with frequent service starting around 06:04 weekdays.
quote: The fastest trains from Menton to Ventimiglia take around 9 minutes, covering a distance of approximately 10 kilometres. On weekdays, the first train leaving Menton is scheduled to depart at around 06:04.

claim: Ventimiglia's Friday market is Italy's largest open-air street market, sprawling along the Roya riverside and seafront with 500+ stalls, 8am–c.4:30pm.
quote: Every Friday, the Ventimiglia seafront becomes a shopping crossroads with the largest market in Italy.

claim: Bus line 10 from Menton's Gare Routière reaches Sainte-Agnès in roughly 40 minutes.
quote: The No. 10 Menton-Sainte-Agnès bus service departs from the Gare Routière de Menton and arrives in Sainte-Agnès in around 40 minutes.

claim: Sainte-Agnès sits at 800 m and is officially the highest coastal village in Europe, classed among France's Plus Beaux Villages.
quote: At 800m above sea level, the utterly beautiful mountain village of Sainte-Agnes is the highest coastal village in Europe.

claim: Fort Sainte-Agnès, a Maginot Line bunker with 2,000 m² of galleries under 55 m of rock, opens Wed–Sun in season with tours at 10:15, 14:15 and 16:00.
quote: It buries itself under more than 55 meters of rock with 2,000 m² of galleries and underground chambers.

claim: Cap Moderne (Villa E-1027, Le Corbusier's Cabanon, Étoile de Mer) is visitable only by guided tour, ~2.5 hours, €15, meeting at the SNCF Cap-Martin Roquebrune station; four daily tours Apr–Oct.
quote: From April 1st to October 31, 2026, the Hangar opens 9:30 am - 5:30 pm with 4 guided tours per day (10 am, 11 am, 2 pm and 3 pm).

claim: The Promenade Le Corbusier / Sentier littoral du Cap Martin is a 4.7 km, ~50 m elevation easy coastal walk linking Carnolès to Cabbé past Cap Moderne.
quote: This 4.7-kilometer one-way hike, with a modest difference in altitude of around 50 meters, is easy to access, making it ideal for families.

claim: Zou! bus 600 (formerly 100) runs Nice–Monaco–Menton every 10–15 minutes on weekdays, €2.10 contactless, serving Èze-sur-Mer, Cap-d'Ail and Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.
quote: One bus every 10 to 15 minutes during weekdays... Open Payment (contactless): €2.10 via NFC card or mobile wallet.

claim: Bus 600 only stops at Èze-sur-Mer on the coast; reaching the hilltop Èze village requires a transfer to Lignes d'Azur bus 83 (15 min climb).
quote: To reach Èze village from Eze-sur-Mer, you can take Lignes d'Azur bus 83, which takes about 15 minutes.

claim: Monaco's Jardin Exotique reopened on 30 March 2026 after a six-year, €18M renovation, adding a children's garden, picnic area and snack bar.
quote: The Exotic Garden officially reopened to the public on March 30, 2026, after six years of closure. The renovation cost over 18 million euros and lasted six years.

claim: Monaco's Prince's Palace Grand Apartments open to the public from 30 March to 15 October 2026.
quote: The Prince's Palace Grand Apartments will be open to the public from Monday March 30, 2026 until Thursday October 15 inclusive.

claim: The Musée Océanographique, founded by Prince Albert I in 1910, anchors the Rocher with its aquarium and panoramic terrace.
quote: Founded in 1910 by Prince Albert I, this museum houses a world-renowned aquarium, unique scientific collections, and a terrace offering one of the most stunning panoramas on the French Riviera.

claim: Zou! bus line 6 from Menton Gare Routière climbs to Castellar (Grande Croix terminus) via Le Baousset.
quote: The first stop of the 6 bus route is Gare Routiere and the last stop is Castellar Grande Croix.

claim: Castillon perches at 706 m as a craft village overlooking the Caramel viaduct's 13 arches; Castellar is the last French perched village before Italy with parallel streets and arched 'traverses'.
quote: At 706 metres elevation, this craft village features stone houses with Provençal green shutters. The nearby Caramel Viaduct displays 13 impressive arches.

claim: Gorbio's village square is dominated by a 1713 elm listed among France's 100 most remarkable trees.
quote: It features an elm tree from 1713 in the village square, which is a magnificent tree and the pride of the local population.

claim: The Marché des Halles (covered market) on Quai de Monléon, between the port and old town, is open daily 8am–1pm year-round with ~30 indoor merchants plus 15–25 seasonal outdoor producers.
quote: Le marché municipal centenaire entre le port et la vieille ville… une trentaine de commerçants chaque jour… A l'extérieur, selon la saison, entre 15 et 25 producteurs ou revendeurs. Ouvert tous les jours de 8h à 13h.

claim: Tripadvisor visitors note Mondays at Les Halles are quieter as not all stallholders are present.
quote: open daily until 1pm, except Mondays when not all dealers are on site

claim: D'AQUI in Menton serves the full Niçoise/Mentonnais street-food canon — socca, pissaladière, pichade and mini barbajuans — in one casual spot.
quote: Socca, pissaladière et pichade, mini barbagiuàn : un délice.

claim: D'AQUI ranks #3 of 248 restaurants in Menton on Tripadvisor and is praised for fresh-to-order socca with strong value.
quote: ranked #3 of 248 restaurants in Menton… socca is made fresh to order and arrives steaming on the table

claim: Maison Herbin, the artisanal jam-maker at 2 rue du Vieux Collège in the old town, has been cooking Menton-lemon jam in copper pans since 1974 and runs 180–200 varieties.
quote: 180 and 200 different varieties of jam, all made before your very eyes… 2 rue du vieux collège, Menton

claim: Local news Nice-Presse calls Mitron Bakery (8 rue Piéta) Menton's best tarte au citron: a crust from house-milled heritage-grain flours and a cream made only from local lemon juice without crème pâtissière.
quote: une crème de fruit faite exclusivement à partir du jus local, sans crème pâtissière, avec une pâte sablée à partir de farines produites pour la maison

claim: Mitron Bakery is chef Mauro Colagreco's (Mirazur) take-away bakery in Menton, serving the Mirazur ecosystem's bread, viennoiseries and its prize-winning Menton-lemon panettone.
quote: imagined by chef Mauro Colagreco… panettone with Menton lemon was elected champion of France 2021 in the 'creative' category

claim: Au Baiser du Mitron, located inside the Halles at 5 Quai de Monléon, sells a classic tarte au citron de Menton on shortbread — a one-stop pairing with the market visit.
quote: Au Baiser du Mitron – Marché des Halles-5 Quai de Monleon, 06500 Menton… Tarte au Citron de Menton (classic lemon tart on shortbread)

claim: Vinum Veritas is the go-to old-town wine bar with a barrel-table terrace, bruschette, charcuterie and cheese boards.
quote: Le bar à vin parfait à Menton… wooden barrels serving as tables on the terrace

claim: Le Cercle des Marins Disparus is a wine/beer/spirits cave with a terrace right on the Garavan port — the most marina-side aperitif option.
quote: cellar of wines, beers and spirits… welcomes you to its terrace in the port of Garavan

claim: Biera d'Aqui has relocated to Les Sablettes facing the sea, with 18 local beers on tap, a large terrace and a kitchen built on family recipes — the new sea-view aperitif spot in town.
quote: déménage face à la mer… dix-huit bières locales… grande terrasse

claim: Bellet AOC, in the hills above Nice, is the closest vineyard to Menton; its whites lean on Vermentino (locally Rolle) and rosés on the indigenous Braquet — what to ask for at any local wine bar.
quote: Bellet… Vermentino, a variety originally from Liguria… Braquet, a red grape indigenous to the Alpes-Maritimes, is the main grape used in a Bellet rosé

claim: ProvenceLovers' Menton picks for a light pre-dinner lunch: Le Petit Port (shady terrace above the old port, Provençal small plates), L'Orangerie (pedestrian-street terrace) and Pasta Piemonte (fresh pasta and Menton-lemon ravioli on the path between station and old town).
quote: Le Petit Port… shady, leafy terrace at the foot of the old town… L'Orangerie… shady terrace… Pasta Piemonte… incredible Menton lemon ravioli

claim: SNCF Connect's Menton food guide singles out barbajuan (fried chard-and-cheese ravioli), pissaladière and the citron de Menton IGP as the five must-try local specialities visitors should track down.
quote: Top 5 des spécialités gastronomiques de Menton

claim: Maison Herbin opens Mon–Sat 9:30–12:30 & 14:00–19:00 and Sun 10:00–12:30 & 15:00–18:00 — usefully open Sunday afternoons when most Menton food shops close.
quote: Lundi au Samedi : 9h30-12h30 / 14h-19h… Dimanche : 10h-12h30 / 15h-18h

claim: The 2026 Fête du Citron in Menton runs 14 February to 1 March 2026 — outside any late-May trip window.
quote: 14 février au 1er mars 2026

claim: Zou! / Zest bus line 15 connects Menton Gare Routière to Castillon (and continues to Sospel), reaching Castillon in about 30 minutes.
quote: The No. 15 Menton-Castillon-Sospel bus service departs from the Bus station and reaches the village of Castillon in around 30 minutes.

claim: Zou! / Zest bus line 7 runs Menton Gare Routière ↔ Gorbio, with a ~21-minute trip and 31-33 stops.
quote: The 7 bus has 31 stops departing from Gorbio and ending in Menton Gare Routière... total trip duration for the route is approximately 21 minutes.
